briefFidelity: The brief is FILIGREE: delicate, fine, fragile, hairline, provisional, thread rather than structure, and — its one emphatic prohibition — 'nothing heavy, nothing solid, no filled mass anywhere.' Blind, before reading it, I described this work as 'drafted geometry — a compass-and-straightedge construction, a rose window, a ritual seal, an architectural plan,' and I called 9190's interior 'a woven grey mush.' I did not once reach for delicate, fragile, thread, hairline or provisional. That is the finding, and I could not have been anchored into it. Roughly half the collection does deliver the register: 9906 is a genuinely lacy hexagonal snowflake, 10443, 9727, 10085 and 9369 are quiet, airy and disturbable. The other half contradicts it. 9190 neutral is a tangled cream field that fills its star frame edge to edge and at browse size is a solid textured lozenge; 10980 is a full heavy mandala of circle plus star plus square ring plus outer frame; 9548 is a thick chunky wreath of two dozen squares; 10264 stacks large translucent squares whose overlaps accumulate into grey tonal plates, which is the nearest thing on these sheets to literal filled mass. None of those four feels provisional or as though it could be disturbed. Two further seeds are not radial figures at all: 10801 is a rectilinear slate frame with pale squares scattered at the corners, and 10622 is an off-centre scatter with no rotational centre, where the brief specifies a radial figure and says tokens differ in its symmetry. And 'contrast kept low' is not met by the bone ink — near-white bone on near-black in 9190, 10980 and 9548 is a hard bright contrast, and that is precisely what converts thread into structure. The material is right throughout and the palette is exactly right; the register is wrong for the densest third to half of the collection, on the brief's most emphatic line. Gate fails.
composition: Composition is genuinely good where the density is right. There is real focal hierarchy in the mid and sparse seeds: 10443 puts a cream diamond around a slate hexagon around three dots, a clean three-step read; 10085 sets one large slate square against one large cream hexagon and lets a single nested square and three dots carry the incident; 9369 hangs two thin rings off the left over a dim ghosted rosette, which is the most confident use of the frame on the sheet because it dares to be asymmetric and leaves real emptiness. 9906 and 9727 build a centre, a ring and a satellite scatter and rank them properly. Where it collapses is at the dense end: 9190 and 10980 are even fields of incident with nothing dominating — the eye lands nowhere and every region is equally busy — and 10264 is an undifferentiated swirl. 10801 is the opposite failure, a frame with debris in it and no subject. Most tokens sit as a centred circular mass in the middle of the tile with the frame unused, which is idiomatic for the radial construction but means the frame is rarely doing compositional work outside 9369, 10622 and 10801.
collectionCoherence: Strong, and the clearest pass on the sheet. Laid out together the twelve are unmistakably one hand and one system: the same two inks, the same flat near-black ground, the same uniform stroke weight, the same closed vocabulary of square, hexagon, circle and diamond, the same two construction rules — nest a shape inside a shape, or copy a shape around a centre — and the same signature habit of dropping a tiny nested detail inside a large otherwise-empty container, which recurs in 10085, 10443, 9369, 9011 and 10801. Even the outliers stay in the family: 10801, which I would not call radial, is still built of the same rotated squares and the same slate-over-bone logic as 9011. Nothing here reads as a folder of unrelated files. If anything the coherence is what makes the density outliers a collection-level problem rather than a per-token one — they are recognisably the same project pushed past the brief.
palette: The palette is the most exact hit against the brief and I named it blind before reading: warm bone or parchment cream and a cool slate blue-grey, over a flat near-black with a slight warm cast, plus dimmed semi-transparent versions of both used to push shapes behind the bright ones. There is no third hue anywhere on any sheet. It looks chosen, not defaulted, and the ground supports the drawing rather than competing with it — the black is dark enough to disappear and warm enough not to read as a void. The depth trick works: in 9369 and 9011 the ghosted rosette sits convincingly behind the bright rings. The one real defect is contrast range against the brief's own instruction to keep it low. The slate half is low-contrast and does read as thread; the bone half does not. On 9190, 10980 and 9548 the bone is bright enough against the black to read as hard structural edge, and on 10264 the accumulating translucent overlaps build up mid-grey tonal plates instead of staying linear.
seedVariation: These are twelve different works, not one work at twelve rotations — the variation problem here is the opposite one, and it is real. Symmetry order genuinely moves: 9906 is 6-fold, 9727 reads 5-fold, 9011 and 9548 run 8-to-12-fold, 10980 is 8-fold, and 10622, 10801 and 10264 abandon rotational symmetry entirely. That axis is exactly what the brief asked for. The problem is the second, unbriefed axis: element count spans from 10085 and 10443, which carry about half a dozen shapes each, to 9190 and 10980, which carry many dozens and become texture. That is a far wider spread than 'how far its threads extend,' which is reach, not count. The consequence is that the collection stops holding one register: 10443 and 9190 side by side do not read as two states of one project's density, they read as a filigree and a woven plate. The system is one system; the intensity is not one intensity, and it is the intensity that the brief was written about.
thumbnailSurvival: Judged on the 120 sheets alone, nine of twelve survive as distinct silhouettes and three do not, and the failures sit at both ends of the density axis. Surviving strongly: 9906 keeps its hexagonal snowflake outline, 10443 reads as a crisp diamond-and-hexagon icon, 9011 and 9727 keep a legible star-with-satellites, 10622 keeps its tilted scatter. Surviving as texture rather than as drawing: 9190, 9548, 10264 and 10980 each hold a distinct outer shape but their interiors turn to undifferentiated mush, which the 256 sheets confirm is genuine fine detail being lost rather than a rendering fault. Failing: 9369 is two thin grey outlines on black and very nearly disappears, 10085 reads as an almost blank tile with a wire hexagon in it, and 10801 reads as an empty square frame. So at the size the collection is actually browsed, the twelve do still look like twelve things, but three of them look like nothing much, and four of them look like the brief's forbidden mass rather than like thread.
marketResponse: Delivered, and delivered exactly as claimed — this is the strongest axis on the sheet and I identified the mechanic blind. The brief says the market expands and contracts the figure's reach, opening out in recovery and drawing in under stress, carried by geometry rather than weight. That is precisely what the state rows do, and stroke weight is visibly constant across all three rows, so the change really is geometric. Stress contracts hard and sheds outer material: 9190 collapses from an edge-filling scribble to a small pale rosette inside a thin dark square with a wide black margin, 9011 becomes a bare slate star with a small cream knot and far more emptiness than ink, 9548 loses its entire outer ring of squares, 9369 halves its main ring and drops most of its nested circles. Recovery overshoots neutral: 9190 fills the tile corner to corner, 9548 regrows the square ring thicker than neutral, 9369 blows its circle up until it nearly touches the tile bottom and stacks a third satellite ring, 9011 adds a second outer frame. It is fully visible at 120 and unmistakable — stress tiles are small quiet objects marooned in black, recovery tiles press to the border. No complaint here at all.
tokenIdentity: Preserved cleanly. Across all three rows each seed keeps its motif, its symmetry order, its colour assignment and its layout, so it reads as one object at three exposures rather than as three objects. 9369 is the two-rings-with-nested-circles-over-a-ghost-rosette token in neutral, stress and recovery alike, and its rings stay anchored to the left in all three. 9548 keeps its slate rosette core and its square-orbit logic whether the orbit has few squares or many. 9190 keeps its rotated-square star frame and its cream interior tangle at every scale. 9011 keeps its slate twelve-point star and cream inner knot. Nothing becomes a different object under drawdown, and no seed swaps its ink assignment between states. The one mild caveat is 9190 stress, which strips so much interior that a viewer meeting it cold might not connect it to 9190 recovery — but the frame geometry still identifies it, so I would not call that a failure.
artifacts: Modest and mostly at the frame edge. Elements cross or touch the tile boundary in the recovery row, which is expected given the expansion mechanic but is not handled: 9011 recovery runs off the left edge, and 9190 recovery presses hard into all four edges with strokes visibly meeting the border. In the neutral seed sheet, 9727 has a small diamond bisected by the right tile edge, which reads as a mistake rather than as a deliberate crop, and 10622 and 10801 push squares into the corners. The other artifact is density-driven rather than geometric: 9190's neutral and recovery interiors and 10980's centre lose their individual squares into a woven grey mush, and 10264's stacked translucent squares accumulate into tonal plates the linework was presumably not meant to produce. Otherwise the rendering is clean — strokes are even, joins are correct, there is no aliasing damage or vanishing stroke even at 120, and no token is empty or half-drawn.
reasoning: The gate decides this. On palette, market response, token identity and coherence the work is genuinely accomplished, and its expand-contract mechanic is one of the clearest state responses I could ask for — I identified it blind, in those words, before reading the brief. But the brief commissioned FILIGREE and glossed it unambiguously: delicate, fine, fragile, hairline, provisional, thread rather than structure, nothing heavy, nothing solid, no filled mass anywhere. Blind, with no knowledge of that text, I described the work as drafted architectural geometry, a compass-and-straightedge construction, a ritual seal, and I named one seed's interior a woven grey mush. Not one delicacy word occurred to me. That disagreement is the evidence, and re-reading the sheets against the brief confirms rather than softens it: 9190, 10980, 9548 and 10264 are dense enough to read as mass at browse size and could not be described as disturbable, 10801 and 10622 are not radial figures at all, and the bone ink on near-black is not the low contrast the brief asked for. The collection's widest axis of variation is element count, which the brief never asked for, and it is exactly the axis that destroys the commissioned register at its top end while leaving 10085 and 10801 as near-empty tiles at its bottom. Half a collection reading as filigree is not a filigree collection, and this would be committed permanently as the answer to that brief. I am refusing it for being heavier than commissioned, not for failing to be some other artwork.
wouldChange: Cap the density, and cap it as a hard bound on the generator rather than as a taste applied per seed. Concretely: (1) Set a ceiling on total element count and on stroke-coverage per tile calibrated so that the busiest token sits near 9727 or 9906, not near 9190 — 9190, 10980, 9548 and 10264 all need roughly half their elements removed, and the removal should come from the repeated ring and interior tangle, not from the containing figure. (2) Forbid accumulated opacity from translucent overlaps summing past a low threshold, which is what turns 10264's stacked squares into tonal plates; clamp the composite so overlaps stay linear. (3) Lower the bone ink toward the slate — pull it off near-white to a dimmer parchment so bone and slate sit within a narrow band, which is what the brief means by keeping contrast low and is what would make the lines read as thread instead of edge. (4) Require every token to have a rotational centre, since the brief specifies a radial figure and says tokens differ in its symmetry; 10801 and 10622 should be regenerated as radial rather than shipped as scatters. (5) Raise the floor at the sparse end so 10085 and 10801 are not near-blank at 120 — add a second order of nested detail rather than more elements, which keeps them light while giving the thumbnail something to hold. (6) Inset the composition bounds so the recovery expansion has margin to grow into, which fixes 9011 and 9190 recovery running off the edge and 9727's diamond bisected by the right border. I would keep the palette, the state mechanic and the nesting vocabulary untouched — they are the parts that already answer the brief.
